name: Fogo Island Inn
insider_take: This architectural marvel sits on stilts above the rugged North Atlantic coastline, where icebergs drift past your window and the Northern Lights dance overhead.
whats_special: Fogo Island Inn is built entirely by local craftspeople using traditional techniques, with each of the 29 rooms featuring handmade quilts and furniture crafted by island artisans. The hotel operates as a social business, with all profits reinvested back into the community. You'll find one of the most remote luxury experiences on Earth, where the nearest traffic light is 240 miles away.
pro_tip: Visit between May-September for iceberg season when massive bergs drift down "Iceberg Alley," or come in winter for spectacular Aurora Borealis displays and the chance to spot snowy owls.
dont_miss: The island's artist studios scattered across the landscape, including the iconic Squish Studio that appears to balance precariously on the rocky shore. Take a boat tour to spot humpback whales, or explore the 400-year-old fishing village of Joe Batt's Arm where Newfoundland traditions remain beautifully intact.
pros: Stunning contemporary architecture with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the North Atlantic
Award-winning culinary program featuring local Newfoundland ingredients and hyper-local cuisine
Unique cultural immersion experience with community-based art and craft workshops
Exceptional spa treatments incorporating local seaweed and sea salt therapies
Personalized service with intimate 29-suite property ensuring exclusive attention
cons: Remote island location requires planning for travel logistics and weather dependencies
Limited dining and entertainment options outside the hotel property
